title: Boss: the compose doctor
summary: Three Compose tickets on a real Docker Engine: a file Compose refuses, a service that died overnight, and an up --wait that never finishes.

steps.title: Before anyone runs up
body: Compose tickets arrive as symptoms: "it won't even start", "something died last night", "CI hangs at `up --wait`".
Each ticket below opens its own machine with a **real Docker Engine** and **Docker Compose**, with the stack in
`~/shop`. Reach for `docker compose config`, `ps -a`, `logs --since/--tail`, `docker inspect` and `up --wait`.

steps.title: Ticket 1: "Compose won't even load it"
prompt: A real Docker Engine with Compose runs in this terminal. `cd ~/shop && docker compose config` fails.
Fix `~/shop/compose.yaml` until Compose accepts it (the API image is `shop/api:1.1`), and provide the database
password the file asks for **without writing it into `compose.yaml`** (the value is in `~/shop/NOTES.md`). Then
`docker compose up -d --wait` must bring up all three services, and `curl http://localhost:8080/` prints `web 1.0`.

checks.name: compose config accepts it
checks.fail: `docker compose config` still reports a problem: fix them one at a time.

checks.name: the password comes from .env, not compose.yaml
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && grep -q '^DB_PASSWORD=..*' .env && ! grep -q example-staging-pw compose.yaml && grep -q '\${DB_PASSWORD' compose.yaml
checks.fail: Keep `${DB_PASSWORD:?...}` in `compose.yaml` and put `DB_PASSWORD=...` in `~/shop/.env` (which stays out of Git).

checks.name: all three are up
checks.fail: Not all services are up. `docker compose up -d --wait`.

hints: `docker compose config` stops at the first problem: fix it and run it again.
Three problems: a required variable, a service with no `image`, and a network name that is not declared.
`echo DB_PASSWORD=example-staging-pw > .env`, add `image: shop/api:1.1` to `api`, and use `front` (declared) instead of `frontend`.
solution: sed -i 's/^  api:$/  api:\n    image: shop\/api:1.1/; s/networks: \[frontend\]/networks: [front]/' compose.yaml
steps.explain: `docker compose config` is Compose's linter: it resolves variables, validates the schema and cross-references (networks, volumes, depends_on) before anything runs. `${VAR:?message}` turns a forgotten secret into a clear error instead of an empty password, and keeping the value in `.env` (git-ignored) keeps it out of the repository.

steps.title: Ticket 2: "something died last night"
prompt: A real Docker Engine with Compose runs in this terminal. The `~/shop` stack ran all night; this morning jobs are piling
up. Investigate with Compose, then fix it:
1. write the name of the **service** that stopped into `~/answers/service.txt`;
3. write the **error line** it logged into `~/answers/error.txt`;
4. fix it the way its error message says, without editing `compose.yaml` (it reads the setting from a variable), and
bring it back so it stays up.

checks.name: service.txt names the service
checks.fail: Not the service that stopped. `docker compose ps -a` shows every service, stopped ones too.

checks.name: exit.txt has its exit code
checks.fail: Not its exit code. `docker compose ps -a` shows `Exited (CODE)`; `docker inspect -f '{{.State.ExitCode}}'` prints it.

checks.name: error.txt has the error line
checks.fail: Not the error line. `docker compose logs --no-log-prefix worker` (add `--tail 20` or `--since 1h` on a busy service).

checks.name: the worker is up and idle
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && docker compose ps --format '{{.Service}} {{.State}}' worker && docker compose logs --no-log-prefix worker | tail -n 1
checks.fail: The worker is not running and idle yet. Its error says which setting to raise; `compose.yaml` reads it from a variable.

checks.name: compose.yaml is unchanged
checks.fail: Leave `compose.yaml` as it is: set the variable in `.env` (or the shell).

hints: `docker compose ps -a` lists stopped services with their exit code.
`docker compose logs --no-log-prefix --tail 20 worker` shows its last lines.
The error says to raise `QUEUE_MAX`: `echo QUEUE_MAX=20 > ~/shop/.env`, then `docker compose up -d worker` recreates it with the new value.
solution: docker compose logs --no-log-prefix worker | grep ERROR > ~/answers/error.txt
steps.explain: A stopped service is easy to miss: `docker compose ps` hides it, `ps -a` shows it with its exit code. `logs --tail`/`--since` cut a night of output down to the lines that matter. Changing an environment value needs a **recreate**, not a restart, and `docker compose up -d SERVICE` does exactly that when the resolved config changed. A `restart: on-failure` policy would have retried, but only a fix stops the crash.

steps.title: Ticket 3: "CI hangs at up --wait"
prompt: A real Docker Engine with Compose runs in this terminal. CI runs `docker compose up -d --wait` in `~/shop`, and it
never succeeds. Try it (it gives up after a while):
Find out why the healthcheck never passes (Docker keeps the output of the last probes) and fix `compose.yaml`, so that
`docker compose up -d --wait` succeeds and every service is up. The API's health endpoint is `/health`.

checks.name: api is healthy
checks.fail: `api` is not healthy. `docker inspect -f '{{json .State.Health}}' shop-api-1 | jq` shows the probe's output.

checks.name: db is healthy and web runs
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && docker compose ps -a --format '{{.Service}} {{.State}} {{.Health}}' db web | sort

checks.name: the healthcheck probes /health
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && docker compose config --format json | jq -r '.services.api.healthcheck.test | join(" ")'
checks.fail: The API's healthcheck should probe its `/health` endpoint on the port it listens on.

hints: `docker compose ps -a` shows `(unhealthy)`; `docker inspect -f '{{json .State.Health}}' shop-api-1 | jq` shows each probe's exit code and output.
`docker compose logs api` says which port the API listens on.
Probe `http://localhost:8000/health` instead of `http://localhost:8080/healthz`, then `docker compose up -d --wait`.
steps.explain: A healthcheck runs **inside** the container, so `localhost` there is the API itself, and the port is the one the app listens on, not the published one. `.State.Health.Log` keeps the last probes' output, which turns "unhealthy" into a concrete error. Because `web` waits for `service_healthy`, one wrong probe blocked the whole stack, and `--wait-timeout` is what keeps CI from hanging forever.
